newsitem.title: CHINA: China nabs hit-and-run driver in U.S. consul death.
newsitem.headline: China nabs hit-and-run driver in U.S. consul death.

text.p: Police in south China have caught a bus driver who fled after his vehicle was involved in a crash that killed a senior U.S. diplomat, Chinese officials said on Wednesday.
"The police notified us this morning that the hit-and-run driver was apprehended," an official of the Guangxi region's foreign affairs office said by telephone.

Philip Lincoln, the U.S. consul-general in the southern China city of Guangzhou, was killed on Monday in a car crash in Guangxi along with Huang Honghui, head of the Beihai city foreign affairs department, and their driver.
Lincoln's vehicle had collided with a long-distance bus that pulled into the oncoming lane to overtake a slower vehicle, the foreign affairs official said.
The bus driver fled on foot after the accident, she said. Local police reached by telephone declined to give details of the case.
Lincoln, a native of Michigan, took up his post in August. He had previously served in Sydney, Seoul and Taipei.
U.S. embassy officials could not immediately give Lincoln's age and hometown.
